title.en: Integer division, inverse products and zero

text.en: A balance has a total change of minus 24 points after four equal rounds. Rani uses multiplication to check the change in each round.

To solve a ÷ b, ask what number multiplied by the non-zero divisor b gives a. Equal signs give a positive quotient and different signs give a negative quotient when both values are non-zero. Zero divided by a non-zero number is zero. A divisor of zero makes division undefined.
Ask what number multiplied by four gives minus twenty-four.
The signed product checks the quotient of minus six.
Two negatives give a positive quotient. Check six times minus four.
Four times zero makes zero. Nothing multiplied by zero makes four.
Seven times minus five is minus thirty-five.

why.en: Different signs give a negative quotient.

text.en: Minus seven times five is minus thirty-five.

why.en: Equal signs in the original division give a positive quotient.

prompt.en: How do you check −18 ÷ (−3), and why can you divide zero by 3?

points.en: Check a quotient by multiplying by the divisor.
